name: Ssu-k’ung Shu
bio: Ssu-k’ung Shu is dated by Giles to the 8th century AD. His poem here is a farewell to a friend.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Oh Stay
poems.author: Ssu-k’ung Shu
poems.text:
We shall meet, I believe you, again;
Yet to part! — such a beautiful night
Shall friendship and wine ask in vain
What a head-wind would take as its right?

poems.title: To a Friend Bound North After the Rebellion
poems.author: Ssu-k’ung Shu
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
In dangerous times we two came south;
Now you go north in safety, without me.
But remember my head growing white among strangers,
When you look on the blue of the mountains of home.
. . . The moon goes down behind a ruined fort,
Leaving star-clusters above an old gate . . .
There are shivering birds and withering grasses,
Whichever way I turn my face.
